title: Friend Circles

examples.explanation: At first 1 and 2 aren't connected (N). After 1–2 and 3–4 become friends, 1 and 2 share a circle (Y), but 2 and 3 don't yet (N). The last line links the two circles, but there are no questions after it.
3 knows 2 and 2 knows 1, so 3 and 1 are in the same circle.

hints: Running a BFS for every question is O(n + m) per question. Is there a structure that merges groups and answers "same group?" quickly?
Union-find (disjoint set union) gives every group one representative. Two students share a circle exactly when their representatives are equal.
Use path compression (or path halving) and union by size. Together they make each operation almost O(1).
